en.bing: Microsoft Bing is a search engine owned and operated by Microsoft, and developed by Microsoft AI. The service traces its roots back to Microsoft's earlier search engines, including MSN Search, Windows Live Search, and Live Search. Bing offers a broad spectrum of search services, encompassing web, video, image, and map search products, all developed using ASP.NET.
en.brave: Brave is a free and open-source web browser which was first released in 2016. It is developed by US-based Brave Software, Inc. and based on the Chromium web browser. Brave is marketed as a privacy-focused web browser and includes features such as built-in advertisement blocking, protections against browser fingerprinting and a private browsing mode that integrates the Tor anonymity network. Brave also incorporates its own advertising through a rewards system based on cryptocurrency, which allows users to earn Basic Attention Tokens (BAT) by opting-in to view ads served through its ad network. While Brave has been praised for its privacy protections and features, it has faced criticism over early plans to replace publisher's ads with its own and missteps surrounding its handling of affiliate links and privacy vulnerabilities in its private browsing mode.
en.google: Google Search is a search and answer engine operated by Google LLC. Launched in 1998 as the company's inaugural product and mostly developed by the company's co-founders, Larry Page and Sergey Brin, it allows users to search for information by entering keywords or queries into a search box on its website or applications, with results indexed by PageRank and other proprietary algorithms. Its homepage is recognized for its minimalist design, with the Google logo or a variant positioned above the search box on an otherwise mostly blank, white screen. Since the AI boom in the 2020s, the service has been heavily integrated with generative artificial intelligence technology through features such as AI Overviews and AI Mode. As a significant vehicle for Google's online advertising business, at the top of the search engine results page is often a sponsored result section.
en.wikidata: Wikidata is a collaboratively edited multilingual knowledge graph hosted by the Wikimedia Foundation. It is a source of open data released under the Creative Commons CC0 public domain dedication. It is for the use of both Wikimedia and external projects. Launched in October 2012, it is developed mainly by Wikimedia Deutschland and supplies the interlanguage links and some of the infobox data used by Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. Wikidata is a wiki powered by the software MediaWiki, including its extension for semi-structured data, the Wikibase. As of early 2025, Wikidata had 1.65 billion item statements. As of October 2026, Wikidata held more than 123 million data entities, such as items, properties and lexemes.
en.wikipedia: Wikipedia is a free online encyclopedia written and maintained by a community of volunteer editors, known as Wikipedians, through open collaboration and the wiki software MediaWiki. Founded by Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger in 2001, Wikipedia has been hosted since 2003 by the Wikimedia Foundation, an American nonprofit organization funded mainly by donations from readers. Wikipedia is the largest and most read reference work in history.

fr.bing: Microsoft Bing, est un moteur de recherche élaboré par la société Microsoft.
fr.brave: Brave est un navigateur web open source disponible sur Microsoft Windows, macOS et Linux ainsi que sur iOS et Android. Il a pour objectif de protéger la vie privée de ses utilisateurs en bloquant par défaut les pisteurs et en permettant la navigation privée via le réseau Tor. Le logiciel, fondé sur Chromium, est développé par l’entreprise américaine Brave Software depuis 2016.
fr.google: Google, connu sous Google Search, est le moteur de recherche le plus populaire dans le monde au début du XXIe siècle. Créé en 1998, c'est le premier produit connu de l'entreprise américaine du même nom.
fr.wikidata: Wikidata est une base de connaissances librement améliorable, conçue pour centraliser les données utilisées par les différents projets du mouvement Wikimédia. Une mise à jour d'une fiche Wikidata se répercute automatiquement sur toutes les pages de projets Wikimédia qui y font appel. Plus largement, Wikidata est destiné à fournir une source commune de données objectives, telles que les dates de naissance de personnalités ou le produit intérieur brut des pays.
fr.wikipedia: Wikipédia est une encyclopédie en ligne collaborative et multilingue créée par Jimmy Wales et Larry Sanger le 15 janvier 2001. Il s'agit d'une œuvre libre, c'est-à-dire qu'elle est en libre accès et que chacun peut la rediffuser gratuitement, telle quelle ou amendée, sous quelques conditions décrites par une licence. Son site web, géré en wiki, permet à tous les internautes d'écrire et de modifier des articles selon des principes collaboratifs, ce qui vaut à l'œuvre d'être qualifiée d'« encyclopédie participative » ou « contributive ».
